---
title: "Assisted MTBC Annotator Pipeline"
author: "AMAP v1.0.0"
date: "`r format(Sys.time(), '%d/%m/%Y')`"

output:
  html_document:
    theme: flatly        # cualquier tema Bootswatch: cerulean, cosmo, darkly, etc.
    toc: true            # activa la TOC
    toc_float:           # flotante (se puede contraer)
      collapsed: false
      smooth_scroll: true
    highlight: tango     # resaltado de código; prueba otros (“monokai”, “textmate”…)
    css: styles.css      # hoja de estilo que añadiremos abajo
    includes:            # inyectamos los logos en la cabecera
      before_body: header.html
params:
  cog_file: "input_cog.txt"
  myco_file: "input_myco.txt"
  summary_file: "input_summary.txt"
  empty_file: "input_noref.txt"

header-includes:
  - |
    <!-- habilita uso de jQuery si no lo carga otro widget -->
    <script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.7.1.min.js"></script>
---

```{js zoom-jquery, echo = FALSE}
$(document).ready(function() {
    // This code requires jQuery to be loaded, which DT::datatable will handle.
    if (window.jQuery) {
        $('body').prepend('<div class="zoomDiv"><img src="" class="zoomImg"></div>');
        // onClick function for all plots (img's)
        $('body').on('click', 'img:not(.zoomImg)', function() {
            $('.zoomImg').attr('src', $(this).attr('src')).css({width: '100%'});
            $('.zoomDiv').css({opacity: '1', width: 'auto', border: '1px solid white', borderRadius: '5px', position: 'fixed', top: '50%', left: '50%', marginRight: '-50%', transform: 'translate(-50%, -50%)', boxShadow: '0px 0px 50px #888888', zIndex: '50', overflow: 'auto', maxHeight: '100%'});
        });
        // onClick function for zoomImg
        $('body').on('click', 'img.zoomImg', function() {
            $('.zoomDiv').css({opacity: '0', width: '0%'});
        });
    }
});

document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  const titleText = document.querySelector("h1.title")?.textContent
                      || "test_AMAP.Rmd";            // ← tu nombre de fichero
  const toc = document.getElementById("TOC");
  if (!toc) return;                                     // por si no hay TOC
  /* Si Tocify ya creó su encabezado, lo sobrescribimos; si no, lo creamos */
  let header = toc.querySelector(".tocify-header");
  if (!header) {
    header = document.createElement("div");
    header.className = "tocify-header";
    toc.prepend(header);
  }
  header.textContent = titleText;
});
```

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)
library(ggpubr)
library(DT)
library(ggsimplestats)
library(stringr)
library(knitr)
library(rstatix) # Added for advanced statistical tests
library(ggrepel) # Added for non-overlapping labels
library(scales) # Added for percentage labels

# Define input files and global variables
cog_summary <- params$cog_file
myco_summary <- params$myco_file
input_sum <- params$summary_file
empty <- params$empty_file

colors <- c("L5"="#995200","L6"="#1eb040","A1"="#d1ae00","A4"="#ff9cdb","A2"="#8ef5c8", "A3"="#73c2ff", "L4"="#ff0000","L1"="#ff3091", "L2"="#001aff", "L3" ="#8a0bd2", "L7"="#fbff00", "L8"="#ff9d00","L9"="#37ff30", "L10"="#8fbda1", "NA"="#808080")
cog_names <- c("A" = "A - RNA processing and modification", "B" = "B - Chromatin structure and dynamics", "C" = "C - Energy production and conversion", "D" = "D - Cell cycle control, cell division, chromosome partitioning", "E" = "E - Amino acid transport and metabolism", "F" = "F - Nucleotide transport and metabolism", "G" = "G - Carbohydrate transport and metabolism", "H" = "H - Coenzyme transport and metabolism", "I" = "I - Lipid transport and metabolism", "J" = "J - Translation, ribosomal structure and biogenesis", "K" = "K - Transcription", "L" = "L - Replication, recombination and repair", "M" = "M - Cell wall/membrane/envelope biogenesis", "N" = "N - Cell motility", "O" = "O - Posttranslational modification, protein turnover, chaperones", "P" = "P - Inorganic ion transport and metabolism", "Q" = "Q - Secondary metabolites biosynthesis, transport and catabolism", "R" = "R - General function prediction only", "S" = "S - Function unknown", "T" = "T - Signal transduction mechanisms", "U" = "U - Intracellular trafficking, secretion, and vesicular transport", "V" = "V - Defense mechanisms", "W" = "W - Extracellular structures", "X" = "X - Mobilome: prophages, transposons", "Y" = "Y - Nuclear structure", "Z" = "Z - Cytoskeleton", "NA"="None")

# Helper function to process combined IDs from input_sum.txt
process_id <- function(id) {
  id <- as.character(id)
  # Handle cases where ID is NA, empty, or starts with an underscore
  if (is.na(id) || id == "" || startsWith(id, "_")) {
    lineage <- "NA"
    genome <- ifelse(is.na(id) || id == "", NA_character_, sub("^_", "", id))
  } else {
    # Split by the first underscore
    parts <- str_split(id, "_", n = 2)[[1]]
    lineage <- parts[1]
    genome <- ifelse(length(parts) > 1, parts[2], NA_character_)
  }
  return(c(lineage, genome))
}

# Read and preprocess data
# COG data - Read robustly to avoid row.names error
datos_cog <- read.table(cog_summary, sep = "\t", dec=".", header = FALSE, fill = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, quote = "", col.names = paste0("V", 1:5))
datos_cog$V2 <- sapply(strsplit(datos_cog$V2, "_"), `[`, 1)

colnames(datos_cog) <- c("Lineages", "genome", "Functional_Category", "Count", "Percentage")
datos_cog$Lineages[is.na(datos_cog$Lineages) | datos_cog$Lineages == ""] <- "NA"
datos_cog <- datos_cog %>% filter(!is.na(Lineages) & Lineages != "")
datos_cog$Functional_Category[datos_cog$Functional_Category == "" | datos_cog$Functional_Category == "NaN"] <- "NA"
datos_cog$sequences <- with(datos_cog, paste(Lineages, genome, sep = "_"))
datos_cog$Percentage<-as.numeric(datos_cog$Percentage)
datos_cog$Count <- as.integer(datos_cog$Count) # Ensure Count is integer

datos_cog <- datos_cog %>%
  # Primero, cuenta las combinaciones únicas de los grupos.
  # Esto crea la nueva columna 'Count'.
  count(Lineages, genome, sequences, Functional_Category, name = "Count") %>%
  
  # Ahora, agrupa por la unidad principal ('sequences') para calcular el porcentaje
  group_by(sequences) %>%
  
  # Crea la columna 'Percentage' dividiendo el conteo de la fila
  # entre el total de conteos para ese grupo 'sequences'.
  mutate(Percentage = Count / sum(Count)) %>%
  
  ungroup()

datos_cog1 <- datos_cog 
lvl_cogs <- c("A","B","C","D","E","F","G","H","I","J","K","L","M","N","O","P","Q","S","T","U","V","NA")
datos_cog1$Functional_Category <- factor(datos_cog1$Functional_Category, levels = lvl_cogs)


# Mycobrowser data - Read robustly
datos_myco <- read.table(myco_summary, sep = "\t", dec=".", header = FALSE, fill = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, quote = "", col.names = paste0("V", 1:5))
datos_myco$V2 <- as.character(datos_myco$V2)
datos_myco$V2 <- sapply(strsplit(datos_myco$V2, "_"), `[`, 1)
colnames(datos_myco) <- c("Lineages", "genome", "Functional_Category", "Count", "Percentage")
datos_myco$Lineages[is.na(datos_myco$Lineages) | datos_myco$Lineages == ""] <- "NA"
datos_myco <- datos_myco %>% filter(!is.na(Lineages) & Lineages != "")
datos_myco$Functional_Category[datos_myco$Functional_Category == "" | datos_myco$Functional_Category == "Unassigned"] <- "NA"
datos_myco$sequences <- with(datos_myco, paste(Lineages, genome, sep = "_"))

datos_myco <- datos_myco %>%
  # Primero, cuenta las combinaciones únicas de los grupos.
  # Esto crea la nueva columna 'Count'.
  count(Lineages, genome, sequences, Functional_Category, name = "Count") %>%
  
  # Ahora, agrupa por la unidad principal ('sequences') para calcular el porcentaje
  group_by(sequences) %>%
  
  # Crea la columna 'Percentage' dividiendo el conteo de la fila
  # entre el total de conteos para ese grupo 'sequences'.
  mutate(Percentage = Count / sum(Count)) %>%
  
  ungroup()

datos_myco$Percentage<-as.numeric(datos_myco$Percentage)
datos_myco$Count <- as.integer(datos_myco$Count) # Ensure Count is integer

# H37Rv reference data
my_myco <- data.frame(
  lineage = c(rep("L4", 11)),
  genome = c(rep("H37Rv", 11)),
    Functional_Category = c("PE/PPE", "cell wall and cell processes", "conserved hypotheticals", "information pathways", "insertion seqs and phages", "intermediary metabolism and respiration", "lipid metabolism", "regulatory proteins", "unknown", "virulence, detoxification, adaptation", "NA"),
  count = c(162, 766, 1042, 240, 149, 936, 271, 198, 15, 239, 13),
  percentage = c(4.018853882411312, 19.00272885140164, 25.8496650955098, 5.953857603572314, 3.696353262217812, 23.220044653932025, 6.722897544033739, 4.9119325229471595, 0.37211610022326963, 5.92904986355743, 0.3225006201935004)
)
merged_data <- merge(my_myco, datos_myco, by = "Functional_Category", all = TRUE)
merged_data$Ratio_Percentage <- (merged_data$Count / merged_data$count) * 100

# Main data for CDS plots - This file needs special ID processing
data_raw <- read.table(input_sum, header = FALSE, sep = "\t", col.names=c("V1", "V2", "V3", "ID"), fill=TRUE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE, quote="")
processed_ids_data <- lapply(data_raw$ID, process_id)
data <- tibble(
  V1 = data_raw$V1,
  V2 = data_raw$V2,
  V3 = data_raw$V3,
  V4 = sapply(processed_ids_data, `[`, 1), # This is the Lineage
  genome = sapply(processed_ids_data, `[`, 2) # This is the Genome
)
data <- data %>% filter(!is.na(V4) & V4 != "")
order_lineages <- rev(c("A4", "A3", "A2", "A1","L10","L9","L6","L5","L4","L3","L2","L7","L1","L8", "NA"))
data$V4 <- factor(data$V4, levels = order_lineages)

# ------------- HELPER FUNCTIONS -------------

# Function to generate statistics tables
generate_statistics_table <- function(data, case_value) {
  data_filtered <- data %>% filter(V1 == case_value) %>% rename(Lineages = V4)
  statistics <- data_filtered %>%
    group_by(Lineages) %>%
    summarise(
      Count = n(), Mean = mean(V2, na.rm = TRUE), SD = sd(V2, na.rm = TRUE),
      Median = median(V2, na.rm = TRUE), IQR = IQR(V2, na.rm = TRUE),
      Min = min(V2, na.rm = TRUE), Max = max(V2, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  
  # Define a base name for the files for this table
  filename_base <- paste0("stats_", case_value)
  
  datatable(
    statistics, extensions = 'Buttons',
    options = list(
      dom = 'Bfrtip',
      buttons = list(
        'copy',
        list(extend = 'csv', filename = filename_base),
        list(extend = 'excel', filename = filename_base),
        list(extend = 'pdf', filename = filename_base),
        'print'
      ),
      pageLength = 14,
      initComplete = JS(
        "function(settings, json) {",
        "$(document.head).append('<link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Roboto:wght@400;700&display=swap\" />');",
        "$(this.api().table().header()).css({'background-color': '#3da68d', 'color': '#fff', 'font-size': '16px', 'font-family': 'Roboto'});",
        "$(this.api().table().body()).css({'font-size': '14px', 'font-family': 'Roboto'});",
        "}"
      )
    ), class = 'cell-border stripe'
  )
}

# Generic function to create scatter plots for different categories
create_scatter_plot <- function(df, category_value, value_col, y_axis_label, plot_title) {
    data_filtered <- df %>% filter(Functional_Category == category_value)
    
    # *** MODIFICATION: Combine boxplot with jitter plot ***
    p <- ggplot(data_filtered, aes(x = Lineages, y = .data[[value_col]], color = Lineages)) +
        geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA, alpha = 0.6) + # Add boxplot outlines
        geom_jitter(alpha = 0.7, width = 0.25) + # Overlay jittered points
        scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
        labs(x = "", y = y_axis_label, title = plot_title) +
        theme_pubr() +
        theme(
            axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
            legend.position = "none"
        )
    
    # If the plotted value is "Count", ensure the y-axis has integer breaks
    if (value_col == 'Count') {
        p <- p + scale_y_continuous(breaks = function(x) unique(floor(pretty(x))))
    }
    
    # Check if there is enough data to perform a statistical test
    if (nrow(data_filtered) > 0 && length(unique(data_filtered$Lineages)) >= 2) {
        # Perform Dunn's test
        stat.test <- tryCatch({
            data_filtered %>%
                dunn_test(as.formula(paste(value_col, "~ Lineages")), p.adjust.method = "BH")
        }, error = function(e) {
            # Return NULL if dunn_test fails for any reason
            return(NULL)
        })
        
        # Add coordinates and p-values only if the test was successful and returned results
        if (!is.null(stat.test) && nrow(stat.test) > 0 && all(c("group1", "group2") %in% names(stat.test))) {
            stat.test <- stat.test %>% add_xy_position(x = "Lineages", step.increase = 0.08)
            
            p <- p + stat_pvalue_manual(
                stat.test, 
                label = "p.adj.signif", 
                tip.length = 0.01, 
                hide.ns = TRUE,
                size = 3.5
            )
        }
    }
    
    return(p)
}
```

# Pathotypr
This section provides a general overview of the dataset composition, showing the distribution of sequences for the identified *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* lineages.

```{r lineage_summary, echo=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.width=14, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# 1. Data Preparation using the 'data' dataframe from input_summary.txt
lineage_summary <- data %>%
  rename(Lineages = V4) %>% # Use V4 as the Lineage column
  mutate(Lineages = ifelse(is.na(Lineages) | Lineages == "", "NA", as.character(Lineages))) %>%
  group_by(Lineages) %>%
  summarise(Count = n_distinct(V3), .groups = 'drop') %>% # Count the number of unique V3 entries (CDS) per lineage
  arrange(desc(Count)) %>%
  mutate(
    Frequency = Count / sum(Count),
    ymax = cumsum(Frequency),
    ymin = c(0, head(ymax, n=-1)),
    labelPosition = (ymax + ymin) / 2,
    label = paste0(Lineages, "\n", round(Frequency*100, 1), "%")
  )

# 2. Plotting
# Plot for Counts
plot_counts <- ggplot(lineage_summary, aes(x = reorder(Lineages, -Count), y = Count, fill = Lineages)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
  labs(title = "Number of Unique CDS per Lineage", x = "Lineage", y = "Number of Unique CDS") +
  theme_pubr() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  expand_limits(y = max(lineage_summary$Count) * 1.1)

# Plot for Frequencies (Donut Chart with repelled labels and connecting lines)
plot_donut <- ggplot(lineage_summary, aes(ymax = ymax, ymin = ymin, xmax = 4, xmin = 3, fill = Lineages)) +
  geom_rect() +
  # Use repel with an anchor point on the donut's outer edge (x=4)
  geom_label_repel(
    aes(x = 4, y = labelPosition, label = label), 
    size = 3,
    show.legend = FALSE,
    segment.size = 0.5,
    segment.color = "grey50",
    nudge_x = 1 # Nudge label away from the anchor point
  ) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  xlim(c(2, 5.5)) + 
  theme_void() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
  labs(title = "Frequency of Unique CDS per Lineage (%)") +
  theme(legend.position = "none", plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))


# Arrange plots side-by-side
ggarrange(plot_counts, plot_donut, ncol = 2, nrow = 1, widths = c(0.6, 0.4))
```

## CDS Correction Summary
This plot shows the proportion of corrected vs. uncorrected CDS for each lineage.

```{r cds_correction_summary, echo=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.width=12, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Data wrangling for the stacked histogram
correction_data <- data %>%
  filter(V1 %in% c("case1_kept", "case4", "case2", "case3")) %>%
  mutate(CorrectionStatus = case_when(
    V1 %in% c("case1_kept", "case4","rv_missing") ~ "Corrected",
    V1 %in% c("case2", "case3")     ~ "Uncorrected"
  )) %>%
  group_by(V4, CorrectionStatus) %>%
  # Correctly summarize by SUMMING the CDS counts (V2)
  summarise(TotalCDS = sum(V2), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  # Calculate percentage for labels
  group_by(V4) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = TotalCDS / sum(TotalCDS),
    Label = if_else(Percentage > 0.05, scales::percent(Percentage, accuracy = 0.1), "")
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Plotting the stacked histogram
p_correction_hist <- ggplot(correction_data, aes(x = V4, y = TotalCDS, fill = CorrectionStatus)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill", stat = "identity") +
  # Add percentage labels inside the bars
  geom_text(aes(label = Label), position = position_fill(vjust = 0.5), size = 3.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    title = "Proportion of Corrected vs. Uncorrected CDS per Lineage",
    x = "Lineage",
    y = "Percentage",
    fill = "Correction Status"
  ) +
  theme_pubr() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

print(p_correction_hist)
```

### Functional Categories by Mycobrowser {.tabset}
This section provides a functional characterization of the annotated CDS based on the Mycobrowser database categories.

#### All Categories
```{r myco_all_cats, echo=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=14, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

  scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Percentage") +
```

## AMAP CDS Stats {.tabset}
This section provides a detailed breakdown of the different CDS-correction cases identified by the AMAP pipeline.  
Each tab shows the distribution of CDS counts for a specific case across all lineages.

The AMAP classification is:

- **Case 1:** Novel CDS not present in the reference H37Rv. 
  - **Case 1 – kept:** CDS missing from the reference annotation; they may be real or artefacts.  
  - **Case 1 – removed:** CDS falsely introduced by Bakta and absent from the reference.
- **Case 2:** Perfect match with the reference.
- **Case 3:** Same start or end as the reference but containing mismatches.
- **Case 4:** CDS coordinates corrected by AMAP.
- **Misssing Rvs:** Genes of H37Rv in the genome not annotated by Bakta and introduced by AMAP.

### CDS Boxplot
```{r cds_boxplot, echo=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=14, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
counts <- data %>% 
  group_by(V4, V1) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(), y_pos = max(V2) + 1, .groups = 'drop')

# Identify V1 groups with more than one V4 level to avoid dunn_test error
valid_comparison_groups <- data %>%
  group_by(V1) %>%
  summarise(n_groups = n_distinct(V4), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  filter(n_groups > 1) %>%
  pull(V1)

stat.test.cds <- NULL # Initialize as NULL

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(V4 = factor(V4)) %>%   # fuerza que sea factor
  droplevels()                  # elimina niveles que no aparecen


if (length(valid_comparison_groups) > 0) {
  # Perform Dunn's test only on valid groups, with error handling
  stat.test.cds <- tryCatch({
    data %>%
      filter(V1 %in% valid_comparison_groups) %>%
      group_by(V1) %>%
      dunn_test(V2 ~ V4, p.adjust.method = "BH") %>%
      add_xy_position(x = "V4", scales = "free_y", step.increase = 0.08)
  }, error = function(e) {
    # If any error occurs during the test, return NULL
    # This prevents the script from stopping
    return(NULL)
  })
}


p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = V4, y = V2, color = V4)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.2), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_text(data = counts, aes(x = V4, y = y_pos, label = n, color = V4), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ V1, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  ggpubr::theme_pubr() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Number of CDS") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", 
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9.5))

# Add significance levels manually only if the test was successful
if (!is.null(stat.test.cds) && nrow(stat.test.cds) > 0) {
  p <- p + stat_pvalue_manual(
    stat.test.cds, 
    label = "p.adj.signif", 
    tip.length = 0.01, 
    hide.ns = TRUE,
    size = 2
  )
}

print(p)
```

### CDS Violinplot
```{r cds_violin, echo=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=14, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
means <- data %>% 
  group_by(V4, V1) %>% 
  summarise(mean_value = mean(V2), y_pos = max(V2) + 1, .groups = 'drop')

p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = V4, y = V2, color = V4)) +
  geom_violin(fill = NA) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 18, size = 3, color = "black") +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2, color = "black") +
  geom_text(data = means, aes(x = V4, y = y_pos, label = round(mean_value, 2), color = V4), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ V1, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  ggpubr::theme_pubr() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Number of CDS") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", 
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9.5)) 

print(p)
```

### Histogram Cases
```{r cds_histo, echo=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.height=4, fig.width=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
filtered_data <- means %>%
  filter(str_starts(V1, "case"))

colores <- c(
  "case1" = "#e41a1c", "case1_keep" = "#13ff03", "case1_remove" = "#377eb8",
  "case2" = "#984ea3", "case3" = "#ffff33", "case4" = "#ff7f00"
)

p <- ggplot(filtered_data, aes(x = V4, y = mean_value, fill = V1)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill", stat = "identity") +
  labs(x = "", y = "Proportion of CDS", fill = "Cases") +
  theme_pubr() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colores) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position="right")

print(p)
```

### CDS Heatmap LogMeanValues
```{r cds_heatmap, echo=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=7, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
p <- ggplot(means, aes(x = V4, y = V1, fill = log(mean_value))) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C", name = "Log Mean Value") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9.5),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9.5),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  labs(x = "Lineages", y = "Cases", title = "Heatmap of Log Mean Values")
print(p)
```
